simple.meaning: מַכְתֵּשׁ (maktêsh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a mortar ; by analogy, a socket (of a tooth).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַכְתֵּשׁ (H4388) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 15:19, with occurrences in Judges, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַכְתֵּשׁ (H4388) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַכְתֵּשׁ (H4388) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַכְתֵּשׁ (maktêsh) / H4388 is traced through Judges 15:19, Proverbs 27:22 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a mortar ; by analogy, a socket (of a tooth)
definitions.full: H4388. maktesh מַכְתֵּשׁ noun masculine mortar (place of pounding, braying; compare Palmyrene proper name, masculine מכתש = contundens Vog No. 97 ) — absolute ׳מ Prov 27:22 (see foregoing); hollow resembling a mortar Judg 15:19 (whence came forth a water-spring; compare GFM), Zeph 1:11 +? Jerusalem, compare Schw ZAW x. (1890), 173 f .
